title: King of Wands Tarot Card Meaning: Upright, Reversed & Love
description: King of Wands upright: leadership, vision, initiative; reversed: impatience, pressure. Love, work, advice and Waite's 1911 text. Ask your question.
h1: King of Wands Tarot Card Meaning
image_alt: King of Wands, 1909 Rider–Waite–Smith card: a crowned king in profile on a throne painted with lions holds a leafy wand upright; a small black salamander at his feet.
capsule: The King of Wands means leadership, vision and initiative: the boldness to turn an idea into something real and bring people with you. Reversed, it can turn overbearing and impatient, or stay all plan, no follow-through. A strong, encouraging card; its risk is control in place of inspiration. The answer is yes: this king sits forward, ready to act.

blocks.heading: What is on the King of Wands card?
paragraphs: A king sits in profile on a high-backed throne, holding a tall wand that sprouts green leaves. Waite writes that "the King uplifts a flowering wand" and wears a "cap of maintenance" beneath his crown (p. 170). The lion, Waite adds, "is emblazoned on the back of his throne" (p. 170).

On the 1909 card the king faces left and sits upright, well forward of the throne back. A pointed yellow crown rests over a red cap; he wears an orange-red robe with a green cape at the shoulders. Black lions and salamanders curled into rings cover the orange throne back, and a small black salamander sits on the step at his feet. Waite gives the card a nature that is "dark, ardent, lithe, animated, impassioned, noble" (p. 170).

blocks.heading: What did Waite write about the King of Wands?
paragraphs: Waite's King is a decent, reliable man, and his card "always signifies honesty" (p. 170). In Waite's reversed reading (p. 170) he is still good, only stricter: severe and austere, yet tolerant.
Waite's extra list gives the reversed card a practical sense, "advice that should be followed" (p. 288).

blocks.heading: What does the King of Wands mean upright?
paragraphs: Leaning forward as if ready to rise, the King of Wands is vision put to work. He stands for leadership, initiative and boldness: someone who sees where things could go, makes the call and brings others along by example rather than orders. He is often read as the entrepreneur, the founder, the natural leader.

When he appears, he asks you to take charge of your own direction. Which decision have you been leaving to others? Honesty is part of this King too, as Waite says (p. 170): he leads in the open, says what he believes and then acts on it.

blocks.heading: What does the King of Wands mean reversed?
paragraphs: Reversed, the King of Wands can turn his fire into pressure: impatience with slower people, an overbearing tone, high expectations nobody can meet, or a big vision with no follow-through. Sometimes it shows the opposite, doubt about whether you have any right to lead.
Waite's reversed King stays good, only severe (p. 170); the harder shades above are a modern reading, not Waite's. Lead by example in one small area, and leave room for others to bring their part.

blocks.heading: What does the King of Wands mean in love?
paragraphs: Mature passion is the theme: knowing what you want, saying it plainly and offering it with warmth and generosity. Unattached, this King favors directness: making the first move honestly instead of playing games, and choosing someone whose plans can stand next to yours.

Between partners, he points toward shared plans and bold gestures, a bond that grows because both people are building something. Upside down, check for control: deciding for two, pushing, or losing patience when someone moves at a different pace. Lead with honesty, not with pressure.

blocks.heading: What does the King of Wands mean for work and money?
paragraphs: This King is at home at the head of things: running a project, founding a business, setting a direction and keeping people motivated. He favors initiative and big-picture thinking; reversed, he warns of micromanaging, or of plans announced loudly and left for others to carry.

As a money card, it means earning through your own vision and drive: income from a venture you lead, confidence when you negotiate your worth. Reversed, it means overconfidence and money decisions made faster than the facts allow.

blocks.heading: What is the advice of the King of Wands?
paragraphs: Make the decision you have been circling, then tell the people it affects, clearly and in your own words. Leading, in this card's sense, means going first and explaining why.

blocks.heading: Is the King of Wands a yes or no card?
The King of Wands as a person and as feelings
paragraphs: Seen in a person, the King of Wands is the born leader: charismatic, honest and bold, quick to take the initiative and sometimes quick to lose patience. He may be a boss, a mentor, a partner, or you whenever you take charge. As feelings, the card means confident, committed interest: strong attraction joined to a wish to build something serious and to say so openly. Reversed, the feeling is still intense but can turn proud or controlling, or cool off through impatience.

blocks.heading: The King of Wands with other cards

pairs.text: Vision and expansion: plans that reach further than before, with you at the front.
Big ideas meet patient craft. The vision needs hours of practice behind it.
A stalemate and the one who can end it. Choose, and say what you chose.
Boldness joined to patience: leadership that persuades rather than pushes.

blocks.heading: King of Wands, The Emperor or King of Pentacles?
paragraphs: Waite seats The Emperor "on a throne, the arms of which are fronted by rams' heads" (p. 84); today that card means structure, rules and stability. The King of Wands leads with vision and enthusiasm, The Emperor with order: one lights the fire, the other builds the walls.

For the King of Pentacles, Waite points to "the bull's head" as a recurring symbol on the throne (p. 254), and the card is read as security and steady abundance. The King of Wands takes risks and inspires; the King of Pentacles keeps and grows.

blocks.heading: Questions to ask yourself about the King of Wands
paragraphs: What decision am I waiting for someone else to make?
Where could I lead by example instead of by pressure?
Which idea of mine deserves a real first step?

faq.q: Is the King of Wands a good or bad card?
faq.a: Good, for most questions. Waite's extra list calls it "generally favourable" (p. 288), and today it stands for courage, vision and honest leadership. Its weak point is pride or pushing too hard, which shows up mainly when the card is upside down.

faq.q: Is the King of Wands a boss or a father figure?
faq.a: It can be either, or neither. It can describe anyone in that position: a manager, a parent, a mentor, an older friend, a partner of any gender, or you. What marks it is the style: bold, warm, decisive and willing to go first.

faq.q: Does the King of Wands mean he loves me?
faq.a: No card can answer for one specific person. In a love question, this King's traditional meaning is mature, committed passion and the wish to build a shared future; upside down, strong emotion mixed with pride. What the person says and does openly will tell you more.

waite.quote: Dark man, friendly, countryman, generally married, honest and conscientious. The card always signifies honesty … Reversed: Good, but severe; austere, yet tolerant.
